conventions.levels: low / mid / high are cost-or-value levels; 'favorable' says which end helps the store (used by the upside scenario; the downside scenario uses the other end).
conventions.tierClass: HRA X/Y/Z city class from data/india-city-tiers.json.
conventions.storeRevenue: Store revenue = min(area × sales per sq ft, area potentialRevenue × captureRate). Without potentialRevenue: min(capacity, SOM × revenueScenarioFactor); without either: capacity × revenueScenarioFactor.

areaSqFt.label: Store area

sources.publisher: Nirmal Bang Equities (broker result update quoting V-Mart Retail disclosures)
sources.title: V-Mart Retail 4QFY25 Result Update
sources.supportingPassage: The retail area of 4.3 msf increased 11.4% YoY. ... Total stores are 497 and 85 of them are UL stores.

areaSqFt.method: V-Mart retail area 4.3 million sq ft / 497 stores = 8,652 sq ft mean store size (Q4 FY25).
areaSqFt.caveat: Network mean of one value retailer, used as a default format size only. Franchise formats are often smaller; override with the planned store area.

revenuePerSqFtYear.label: Benchmark sales density

sources.publisher: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited
sources.title: ABFRL Q4 & FY26 Investor Presentation
sources.supportingPassage: FY26 Update: segment revenue Rs. 4560 Cr ... Area (000s sq. ft.) / stores, Mar 2026: 5,781 / 399.

sources.publisher: Nirmal Bang Equities (broker result update quoting V-Mart Retail disclosures)
sources.title: V-Mart Retail 4QFY25 Result Update
sources.supportingPassage: For FY25, sales per square feet at Rs710 was higher ~11% on YoY basis. (Sales per sqft reported in Rs/month.)

sources.title: Press release: financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2025
sources.supportingPassage: Revenue From Operations 29,815 24,362 22.4% 61,218 ... total retail area of ~12.76 million Sq. Ft

revenuePerSqFtYear.method: low: Pantaloons FY26 segment revenue Rs 45,600 mn / 5.781 mn sq ft = Rs 7,888; mid: V-Mart FY25 Rs 710/sq ft/month × 12 = Rs 8,520; high: Vishal Mega Mart H1 FY26 revenue Rs 61,218 mn × 2 / 12.76 mn sq ft = Rs 9,595 (includes general merchandise and FMCG).
revenuePerSqFtYear.caveat: Listed-retailer network averages, used only as a store-capacity fallback and a plausibility check; not a forecast of sales at a specific site.

captureRate.label: Store capture of area revenue potential
captureRate.rationale: Share of the area's organised apparel revenue potential that one new store wins. low 5% ≈ one of ~20 comparable organised outlets serving the area; mid 10% ≈ one of ~10; high 15% ≈ an anchor store that also draws shoppers from neighbouring PINs (spend outside the area is not counted in potentialRevenue).
captureRate.caveat: No sourced store-level capture benchmark was found; model assumption. Replace with the brand's observed share in comparable catchments.

grossMargin.label: Gross margin

sources.title: Press release: financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2025

sources.publisher: Nirmal Bang Equities (broker result update quoting V-Mart Retail disclosures)
sources.title: V-Mart Retail 4QFY25 Result Update
sources.supportingPassage: For FY25, gross margin at 34.5% was flat YoY.

grossMargin.method: low: Vishal Mega Mart H1 FY26 28.3%; high: V-Mart FY25 34.5%; mid: midpoint.
grossMargin.caveat: Company-level retailer margins. A franchisee's trade margin depends on the brand agreement and is usually lower; override with the brand's margin.

rentPerSqFtMonth.label: Rent

sources.title: Delhi's Khan Market rents rise 8% as demand lifts high-street retail
sources.supportingPassage: Q4 2025 Delhi high-street rents (INR/sq ft/month): Khan Market 1,700-1,800; Connaught Place Inner Circle 1,150-1,250; Lajpat Nagar 290-310; Rajouri Garden 255-265.
sources.usage: Context only: prime high-street rents are far above these bands and are not used in the calculation.

rentPerSqFtMonth.rationale: Blended (ground + upper floor) rent bands for a large-format value apparel store outside prime high streets, by HRA city class.
rentPerSqFtMonth.caveat: No sourced city-tier rent series for mass-format stores was found. These are model assumptions; replace with a site lease quote.

fitOutPerSqFt.label: Fit-out and interiors

sources.title: Office Fit-Out Cost Guide — India
sources.supportingPassage: most markets clustering between INR 5,847 and INR 6,567 ... for a collaborative hybrid workplace
sources.usage: Context only: office fit-out, higher specification than value retail; not used in the calculation.

fitOutPerSqFt.rationale: Value-format apparel fit-out (flooring, lighting, fixtures, HVAC, IT/POS, signage).
fitOutPerSqFt.caveat: No sourced retail fit-out benchmark was found; model assumption. Replace with contractor quotes.

staffMonthlyWage.label: Staff wage

sources.publisher: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
sources.title: Annual Report, Periodic Labour Force Survey 2023-24 — Appendix A, Table (50): average wage/salary earnings during the preceding calendar month by NCO-2015 occupation division, all India
sources.page: A-340 to A-341 (PDF pages 403–404; page footer reads 'Annual Report, PLFS, 2022-23' as printed)
sources.supportingPassage: Average wage/salary earnings (Rs.), NCO division 5 (service and sales workers): rural person 13,072; urban person 15,829; urban male 17,302.

staffMonthlyWage.method: PLFS 2023-24 Table 50, NCO-2015 division 5 (service and sales workers): low = rural person, mid = urban person, high = urban male.
staffMonthlyWage.caveat: All-India average earnings in 2023-24 rupees; not state-specific and excludes employer statutory contributions (see employerOnCostRate).

employerOnCostRate.label: Employer on-costs (PF, ESI, bonus)
employerOnCostRate.rationale: Employer provident fund and insurance contributions plus statutory bonus; applicability depends on establishment size and wage ceilings.
employerOnCostRate.caveat: Model assumption; confirm with payroll advisor.

sqFtPerEmployee.label: Selling area per employee
sqFtPerEmployee.rationale: Staffing density for an assisted-self-service value apparel floor including cashiers and stockroom.
sqFtPerEmployee.caveat: Model assumption; replace with the brand's staffing plan.

utilitiesPerSqFtMonth.label: Utilities, maintenance and housekeeping
utilitiesPerSqFtMonth.rationale: Electricity, common-area maintenance, security and housekeeping.
utilitiesPerSqFtMonth.caveat: Model assumption; electricity tariffs vary by state DISCOM.

marketingRate.label: Ongoing marketing
marketingRate.caveat: Model assumption; brand agreements may fix this.

royaltyRate.label: Royalty / brand fee
royaltyRate.rationale: Ongoing franchise royalty or margin share.
royaltyRate.caveat: Brand-specific; replace with franchise disclosure terms.

depositMonthsOfRent.label: Security deposit
depositMonthsOfRent.rationale: Refundable lease deposit; Indian commercial leases commonly ask several months of rent.
depositMonthsOfRent.caveat: Model assumption; refundable deposit is treated as invested capital and not recovered within 5 years.

inventoryTurnsPerYear.label: Inventory turns
inventoryTurnsPerYear.rationale: Opening stock = benchmark-capacity annual cost of goods / turns.
inventoryTurnsPerYear.caveat: Model assumption; sale-or-return arrangements with the brand can reduce this materially.

preOpeningCosts.label: Pre-opening marketing, training and licences
preOpeningCosts.rationale: Launch marketing, staff training, trade licence and registrations.

revenueScenarioFactor.label: Revenue scenario factor
revenueScenarioFactor.rationale: Same 0.75 / 1 / 1.25 scenario factors used by the existing store forecast (server/market-forecast.cjs).

initialRampFraction.label: Month-1 sales vs steady state
initialRampFraction.rationale: New stores ramp to steady-state sales.

rampMonths.label: Months to steady-state sales
rampMonths.rationale: Linear ramp from the month-1 fraction.

costInflation.label: Annual escalation of rent, wages and utilities

sources.title: Monetary Policy — overview (inflation target)
sources.referencePeriod: Target retained for April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031
sources.supportingPassage: 4 per cent Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation as the target ... with the upper tolerance limit of 6 per cent and the lower tolerance limit of 2 per cent ... retained ... April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031.
sources.usage: low end anchored on the CPI target; mid/high allow for typical lease escalations.

discountRate.label: Discount rate for NPV
discountRate.rationale: Owner's required return for a small retail investment.
discountRate.caveat: Model assumption; set your own cost of capital.

revenueGrowth.label: Nominal same-store sales growth
revenueGrowth.method: low = RBI CPI target (4%, prices only); high = state per-capita NSDP nominal CAGR (full income pass-through); mid = average of the two. Falls back to 4% / 5% / 6% (model_assumption) when the state series is unavailable.

sources.title: Monetary Policy — overview (inflation target)
sources.referencePeriod: Target retained for April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031
sources.supportingPassage: 4 per cent Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation as the target ... with the upper tolerance limit of 6 per cent and the lower tolerance limit of 2 per cent ... retained ... April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031.
